title: Campus Climate Sensor Network
summary: Build a small set of low-cost nodes that measure temperature, humidity, and another carefully chosen environmental variable.
description: The first version would use two or three sensor nodes, a documented calibration check, and a simple dashboard. The team would decide whether air quality, soil moisture, light, or another variable is useful and feasible. Deployment would happen only with permission from the relevant space owner.
impact: Give students a complete hardware-to-data project while producing measurements that can be checked, explained, and improved.

title: Energy Use Visualizer
summary: Create a physical or web-based display that makes an approved energy dataset easier to understand.
description: The team would begin with a public or permissioned dataset, define one audience and one decision the display should support, then prototype a clear visualization. A physical version could use addressable lights or a small screen; a web version could focus on accessibility and mobile use.
impact: Practice turning technical measurements into information that a non-specialist can interpret.

title: Assistive Reminder Device
summary: Prototype a simple, customizable reminder device using light, sound, vibration, or a large physical control.
description: The project would start with interviews or published accessibility guidance rather than guessing at user needs. The first prototype should test one interaction, such as acknowledging a reminder with a large button, and should avoid medical claims or collection of sensitive health information.
impact: Introduce human-centered engineering and accessibility without pretending a classroom prototype is a medical device.

title: Robotics Starter Rover
summary: Build a small rover that can follow a line, avoid an obstacle, or complete another measurable beginner challenge.
description: The team would choose one behavior, document the wiring and code, and create a starter guide another student can reproduce. Advanced features such as mapping or computer vision would be treated as later extensions, not requirements for the first build.
impact: Give new members a shared platform for learning mechanics, electronics, programming, and test design.
